channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: 30% Drop in Levels of Forever Chemicals in England’s Rivers, 49% in Fish – ‘Brilliant to See’
item.description: Two banned forever chemicals have fallen 30% in England's rivers and 49% in the fish that live there. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Choose PFAS-free cookware and outdoor gear when you next replace them. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
item.description: New York's largest electric school bus fleet now serves a South Bronx area with high childhood asthma. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?
item.description: A Somerset farm is testing apple varieties and natural methods to help cider orchards cope with a changing climate. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Buy cider or apple juice from local orchards to keep traditional varieties planted. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Greek coastline cleanup that turned trash into a pollution map
item.description: Volunteers cleaning a small Greek islet logged every item, turning decades of washed-up rubbish into a pollution map. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Join a beach clean and record what you collect; the tallies help trace where pollution comes from. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Animal welfare ballot measures had a strong night in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Voters in several US states passed animal welfare ballot measures, including limits on foie gras, by wide margins. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Farmer Finds Unknown Seeds in His Attic – and Grows an Ancient ‘Miracle’ Grain
item.description: An Italian farmer sowed old wheat seeds found in his attic and revived a near-lost heritage grain. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Tokyo Tackles Trash Troubles with New Generation of Robotic Street Waste Bins
item.description: Tokyo is fitting solar compactor bins and trash-hauling robots to keep busy tourist streets clean. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Carry your litter with you in crowded places until you find a bin with room. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Climbers Lug Endangered and Orphaned Seal Pup Up a Cliff to Safety
item.description: Climbers in Greece carried an orphaned pup of a critically endangered seal up a cliff to safety. How you can help: If you find a lone seal pup, keep your distance and phone a local wildlife rescue. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Scientists found thousands of tiny animals living inside metal-rich rocks on the deep Pacific seabed. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: A Staten Island barbershop is using the trust between barber and customer to support the health of Black men. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Book the routine health check you have been putting off. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney
item.description: A trust is studying whether beavers could return to the River Waveney and improve its health. Evidence: Early research. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Pupils fascinated by space get astronomy lesson
item.description: A Cambridge astronomer visited a primary school to give space-loving pupils an astronomy lesson. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom
item.description: Physicists found a way to steer the magnetic spin of a single atom's nucleus using radio waves. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
item.description: A virus that infected ancestral apes millions of years ago may help explain how the human brain develops. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This Tourette’s wrist device cut tics by a quarter in a UK trial
item.description: A wrist device cut tics by a quarter on average in a UK trial of 121 people with Tourette's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: They Became Pen Pals as Teens, Now 32 Years Later They’re Happily Married
item.description: Two teenagers who met on holiday in Kos in 1994 became pen pals, and 32 years on they are married. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World-First Bone Marrow Transplant Successfully Treats Non-Malignant Disease
item.description: Doctors at a Midwest hospital report a world-first bone marrow transplant that treated a non-malignant disease. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Join a bone marrow donor registry; signing up usually takes only a cheek swab. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: San Francisco Gets its Largest-Ever Gift: $100M for Public Parks From Airbnb Founder
item.description: San Francisco's public parks received a $100 million gift, the largest single donation in the city's history. How you can help: Join a planting or clean-up day at a park near you. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: A modelling study suggests vitamin C may limit cancer-linked chemicals forming in the stomach after meals. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: Lab work links low levels of the amino acid arginine to weaker immune defences against cancer and viruses. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
item.description: Chemical traces in fossil teeth suggest some dinosaurs ate seaweed more than 100 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: The Euclid telescope found 31 quasars from the universe's first billion years, two of them record-bright. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time
item.description: SpaceX caught the top stage of its Starship rocket in mid-air for the first time, a step toward reuse. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Couple with Autism and ADHD Find Passion Cleaning Filthy Street Signs
item.description: A married couple spend their spare time scrubbing grimy street signs clean, and hope to tour the country doing it. How you can help: Pick one neglected spot on your street and give it a clean. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Two of the ‘Last Wild Ecosystems’ Untouched by Humans Are Declared New Sanctuaries
item.description: Two remote Pacific atolls, among the last ecosystems untouched by people, have been declared sanctuaries. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers found a large icy body beyond Pluto that could become the sixth recognised dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dr. King’s Lost Draft of ‘I Have a Dream’ Emerges from a Desk Drawer
item.description: A handwritten draft of Dr King's 'I Have a Dream' speech has resurfaced after six decades in a desk drawer. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Rescues Trapped Neighbors from ‘Biblical’ Florida Flooding
item.description: A Florida man went through floodwater to bring two vulnerable neighbours, one with ALS, to safety. How you can help: Check on elderly or unwell neighbours when severe weather is forecast. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Infant Goes from 110 Seizures a Day to Seizure-Free with Experimental Treatment
item.description: A baby in Dubai who had about 110 seizures a day is seizure-free after an experimental drug. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is rebuilding its visitor economy around tourism that gives back to the island. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, set aside a day to volunteer with a local restoration project. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two Princeton graduates built a system that removes microplastics from water at treatment plants. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Wash synthetic clothes less often and on cooler, shorter cycles to shed fewer fibres. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: China Switches on World’s Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage
item.description: China has switched on the largest liquid-air energy storage plant yet, holding renewable power for later use. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 100-Year-Old ‘Store Mom’ Surprised With Her First Birthday Party
item.description: Store staff threw a first-ever surprise birthday party for a 100-year-old who walks their aisles every day. How you can help: Learn the name of someone you see every day and say hello. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions about twice as fast as humans, a University of Tübingen study found. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: An AI model predicts what a blind man sees through his brain implant, making bionic vision more precise. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A familiar tropical butterfly turns out to be three species, one of them new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
item.description: Experiments suggest Earth's water may have formed in the young planet's hot atmosphere, not arrived on comets. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: What began as a fight to save a tree in Aachen has grown into work on using moss to green city streets. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: Los Angeles has banned oil drilling for good after a decade of pressure from residents living beside wells. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Speak at a local council meeting; steady pressure from residents is what moved this. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
item.description: Each mosquito species is drawn to its own mix of human skin odours and bacteria, a study found. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
item.description: Fossils of a 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago were found in Thailand. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: A young organiser turned his own loss into a peer tutoring programme for refugee students. How you can help: Offer an hour a week of tutoring through a local school or library. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding play corners and family support so that students with children can keep studying. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana guest ranch, autistic people work as guides, wranglers, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew Gardens is moving 1,300 plants to safety so that its Palm House can be renovated. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
